entrypoints.summary: The Flask handler accepts GET and POST requests at /verify_roles and obtains role from the request query string.
The supplied browser client places the user-controlled role value directly into a GET query URL for the local /verify_roles service.

affected_components.role: Reads query role, constructs and parses JSON, and makes the privileged authorization decision.
Builds the browser request URL from the role input.

code_slices.vulnerable: verify_roles obtains role from the query string, filters and regex-checks text built with role interpolation, parses that text with ujson, then checks parsed name and role fields for the privileged branch.

impact.attacker_capability: Potentially cause authorization to consume parsed name and role fields that differ from the textual role representation screened before parsing; a concrete accepted payload is not established in the bundle.
impact.security_effect: Conditional disclosure of the subscription_code environment value through the privileged response branch.

causal_trace.summary: The handler reads the attacker-controlled role query parameter; the supplied client likewise concatenates its role input into the /verify_roles query URL.

Before parsing, the handler removes literal occurrences of superuser, rejects literal spaces and values longer than 30 characters, then interpolates the remaining role text into JSON syntax. It applies a regular-expression check to the constructed text before parsing it.

The handler parses the complete interpolated JSON text with ujson and uses user_data['name'] and user_data['role'] from that parsed object for the authorization decision. Thus the representation inspected by the pre-parse substring/regex checks is not inherently the parsed field representation consumed by authorization.
If the parsed object has name equal to admin and role equal to superuser, the handler returns the subscription_code environment value; all other parsed values receive a non-privileged response.

failure.operation: ujson.loads of JSON text assembled by interpolating the query role, followed by authorization on parsed name and role fields

primary_invariant.statement: Authorization must evaluate the same decoded, structured name and role values that are validated, without constructing JSON from untrusted role text and separately inspecting a pre-parse textual representation.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The handler validates and regex-extracts a string-built JSON representation before ujson parses it, but its privileged decision is made from fields of the subsequently parsed object.

quality.review_notes: Primary handler and client source establish the pre-parse versus post-parse representation mismatch and the conditional disclosure branch. The bundle has no request/response execution trace, exploit payload, dependency-version behavior evidence for ujson, test, or remediation patch. In particular, parser handling needed to demonstrate a concrete bypass is not established.

remediation.invariant_restored: Parse a structured request once, validate the decoded fields that will be authorized, and make the authorization decision only on those validated fields rather than on JSON reconstructed from a role string.
mitigation_classes: elimination of untrusted JSON string interpolation

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Submit a role query value satisfying the handler's visible raw-text restrictions; any ability to alter parsed fields beyond that value is unverified.
data_structure_invariants: The name and role values authorized after parsing must be the same values that were validated.
Untrusted role content must not alter JSON structure during construction.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The handler rejects role values with length greater than 30 and rejects literal spaces.

numeric_domains.width: unbounded application string measured by Python len

state_context.state_machine: Request role text is screened as text, embedded into JSON text, regex-inspected, parsed, then evaluated as parsed authorization fields.
